q: The Lax-Milgram theorem guarantees existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to elliptic PDEs. It states: if a(u,v) is a bilinear form on a Hilbert space H that is continuous and coercive (a(u,u) ≥ α||u||²), then for any f ∈ H*, there exists unique u ∈ H with:
opts: a(u,v) = f(v) for all v ∈ H
exp: Lax-Milgram: under continuity |a(u,v)| ≤ M||u||||v|| and coercivity a(u,u) ≥ α||u||², the variational problem a(u,v) = f(v) ∀v has a unique solution u with ||u|| ≤ ||f||/α. This underlies existence of weak solutions to Poisson, elliptic, and parabolic PDE problems.
